question.text: A null point is found at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> in potentiometer when cell in secondary circuit is shunted by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. When a resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is used for shunting null point moves to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The internal resistance of the cell is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Let potential gradient be x.

For the first case, we can write

εr+5×5=200x ......(1)

and after adding resistance, we can write

εr+15×15=300x .....(2)

From both equations, we get

⇒r=5 Ω
